Managing Valid Texts and Invitations

By the Valid team · Published September 13, 2026

An unexpected compliment text can raise reasonable questions: who sent it, why did it arrive, and how can it stop? Valid texts can include member-shared invitations and activity notifications sent by Valid. Understanding the type of message helps you choose the right next step.

Two different ways a message can arrive

A member can share an invitation using their phone’s message composer. For example, after voting for a contact who has not joined, they may see an Invite prompt and choose whether to send the message. That invitation comes from the member’s phone.

Valid can also send SMS activity notifications through its messaging service. These are separate from invitations a member chooses to send personally. We explain both because it would be inaccurate to say that every text about Valid is manually sent by a friend.

A text does not mean you registered

Members can select people saved in their contacts in polls, including people who have not created a Valid account. A contact match or a vote is not an account registration. Receiving a message by itself does not mean you joined the app.

For the same reason, do not assume an unexpected text proves that a child installed Valid. Start by reviewing the actual message together. If its origin or meaning is unclear, support can investigate using the message and the phone number that received it.

How to stop unwanted messages

For a text sent through Valid’s messaging service, reply STOP when that option is provided. If the message came directly from someone’s personal number, ask that sender to stop or use your phone’s blocking controls. Those are different channels, so stopping one does not necessarily prevent invitations through the other.

You can also email support@validapp.lol. You do not need to install Valid to ask for help. Send the relevant details privately rather than posting a phone number or a child’s information in a public comment.

Be specific about what you want stopped

Stopping texts, removing your information, and excluding your phone number from voting are separate requests. If you want all three, say so clearly. For example: “Please stop Valid texts to my number, remove my information, and suppress my number from voting. I do not want to participate.” Include the affected number privately so support can locate the correct information.

Our approach to unwanted texts should be judged by clear explanations and useful controls. A message about a positive poll can still be unwanted. If messages continue after your request, contact support with the new message and the earlier request so we can investigate.

Read why you received a text from Valid for the main message explanation and our Privacy Policy for information about data use and sharing.
